panels.figure_caption: Preoperative clinical photograph demonstrating right-sided orofacial gangrene. The white arrow depicts the central necrotic ulceration with eschar, purulent discharge, and surrounding indurated erythema extending from the right buccal region to the preauricular area. The findings are consistent with established gangrenous noma in an immunocompromised elderly host.
in_text_mentions: g over the right buccal region, measuring approximately 5 × 4 cm. The central zone demonstrated frank ulceration with undermined necrotic margins, surrounding erythema, and copious purulent discharge with a fetid odor. The overlying skin showed early dusky discoloration indicative of impending cutaneous involvement (Figures 1-2). Maximum inter-incisal opening (trismus) was restricted to 35 mm, which affected the patient's ability to speak clearly or eat comfortably. Ipsilateral submandibular lymphadenopathy was present. The lips, palate, floor of mouth, and contralateral cheek were uninvolved.

B: Lateral-oblique clinical photo of same patient showing gaping right cheek defect; caption-specific noma manifestation. C: Inferior/worms-eye clinical photo showing nasal/septal exposure from noma-related soft-tissue loss. D: Frontal 3D CT of same noma patient showing bony destruction and ankylosis described in caption as noma sequelae. E: Lateral 3D CT of same patient showing right-sided maxillary loss and TMJ ankylosis/fusion from noma.

panels.figure_caption: (a). Marked facial asymmetry, pronounced occlusal cant and right orbital dystopia. (b) and (c) Soft-tissue loss involving right cheek and oral commissure, right upper lip and ala, exposing the vomer and nasal septum. (d) and (e) Computed tomographic images showing right temporomandibular joint ankylosis, right zygomaticomandibular fusion, right ascending ramus hypoplasia and coronoid process hypertrophy (from temporalis contracture),5 loss of the right maxilla and maxillary teeth, vomer and one-third of hard palate.
in_text_mentions: A 20-year-old Laotian woman presented with a large facial defect and bilateral trismus (Fig 1). At 4 years of age, she came down with a high fever. A foul-smelling, fulminating ulcer developed over her right cheek and evolved into a black eschar that ulcerated. She gradually developed temporomandibular ankylosis (“constriction des mâchoires”)10-12 with interlocked left-sided teeth and was unable to open her mouth to feed or talk. She fed by inserting food through the facial defect and manually grinding it against her remaining right mandibular teeth.

Examination and imaging revealed marked facial asymmetry, pronounced occlusal cant, and right orbital dystopia (Fig 1a). Soft-tissue losses involved the right cheek and oral commissure, right upper lip and ala, exposing the vomer and nasal septum, leaving a 4.5 cm by 3 cm defect (Figs 1b and 1c). Bony abnormality included right intra- and extraarticular ankylosis (temporomandibular joint ankylosis and zygomaticomandibular fusion, respectively), loss of the right maxilla and maxillary teeth, vomer and one-third of hard palate, right ascending mandibular ramus hypoplasia, and a hypertrophic coro

nt and zygomaticomandibular fusion released with a horizontal ramus osteotomy, achieving maximal incisal opening (MIO) of 0.5 cm (Fig 2a). The left side was explored (Fig 2b), revealing extraarticular (fibrous) trismus, flattening of the left mandibular condyle, glenoid fossa, and articular eminence. Left condylectomy, coronoidectomy, and fascia lata interposition arthroplasty (Fig 2b) was performed. Complete bilateral release resulted in a larger facial defect measuring 7 cm by 5 cm (Fig 2c). An intraoral orthodontic appliance was fashioned as a bite block to maintain the MIO postoperatively.
